Achar
AY-kar
proper noun
Hebrew ’akar, “to trouble” or “to bring disaster”; a son of Carmi of Judah, called Achan in Joshua, Achar in the Chronicles, the troubler of Israel.

📖 Biblical Definition

Achar, who is Achan, was a son of Carmi of the tribe of Judah, in the line of Zerah, and his name is bound forever to the sin of the camp at Jericho: “And the sons of Carmi; Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the thing accursed” (1Chr 2:7). When Jericho fell, the LORD had commanded that the city and all therein be devoted and accursed, and that none should take of the spoil. But Achan coveted and took a goodly Babylonish garment, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold, and hid them in his tent; and the anger of the LORD was kindled against all Israel, so that they fled before the men of Ai (Josh 7:1). This was sin in the camp: the secret transgression of one man brought defeat and death upon the whole congregation, for Israel was a covenant body and not a heap of severed souls. By lot the LORD found him out, and Joshua said, “Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones” (Josh 7:25). They raised over him a great heap of stones in the valley, which was called the valley of Achor, that is, of trouble, unto this day (Josh 7:26). Here is the doctrine plainly: sin is no private matter, covetousness is idolatry, and the holiness of God will not wink at the accursed thing hidden in the tent. Yet the valley of trouble becomes a door of hope to the penitent (Hos 2:15), for the blood of Christ alone cleanseth the camp.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A son of Carmi of Judah, the troubler of Israel, who took of the accursed thing at Jericho and was stoned in the valley of Achor.

ACHAR, who is Achan, a son of Carmi of Judah, the troubler of Israel.

The name signifies “trouble” or “to bring disaster.”

He transgressed in the accursed thing, taking of the spoil of Jericho.

His sin brought defeat upon all Israel before the men of Ai.

He was stoned in the valley of Achor, named for the trouble he wrought.

📖 Key Scripture

1Chr 2:7 — "And the sons of Carmi; Achar, the troubler of Israel, who transgressed in the thing accursed."

Josh 7:1 — "But the children of Israel committed a trespass in the accursed thing: for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel."

Josh 7:25 — "And Joshua said, Why hast thou troubled us? the LORD shall trouble thee this day. And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire, after they had stoned them with stones."

Josh 7:26 — "And they raised over him a great heap of stones unto this day. So the LORD turned from the fierceness of his anger. Wherefore the name of that place was called, The valley of Achor, unto this day."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A man whose sin is named plainly in Scripture: covetousness is idolatry, and the hidden accursed thing brings trouble upon the whole camp of God.

expand to see more

Achar is no contested doctrine but a warning written in blood. His sin was real sin: he coveted the accursed thing, took it, and hid it in his tent, and the wrath of God fell upon all Israel. The Scripture does not soften it nor make it a misfortune; it names it transgression in the thing accursed (Josh 7:1), and it shows that the secret sin of one defiles the whole body.

The principle to recover is the holiness of God who will not wink at hidden sin, and the covenant solidarity of His people, wherein the camp is troubled by the transgressor in its midst. Covetousness is idolatry (Col 3:5), and no goodly garment nor wedge of gold is worth the trouble it brings. Yet the valley of Achor is made a door of hope (Hos 2:15) to the penitent, for the blood of Christ alone purges the accursed thing and cleanses the camp of God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew ’akar, “to trouble,” Achar names the troubler of Israel who took the accursed thing.

Achar — Hebrew ’akar, “to trouble” or “to bring disaster.”

He is called Achan in Joshua, Achar in the Chronicles.

He was a son of Carmi, of the line of Zerah in Judah.

He transgressed in the accursed thing at Jericho.

The valley of Achor was named for the trouble he wrought.

Usage

"Like Achan, the hidden sin of one believer may bring trouble upon the whole congregation."

"Covetousness is idolatry; no garment of gold is worth the accursed thing it conceals."
